newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners drive Louisiana crude prices higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners drive Louisiana crude prices higher.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes were firmer late Monday as refiners emerged to buy scarce light, sweet barrels, driving Louisiana crude prices higher.
The tight Brent/West Texas Intermediate arbitrage, coupled with refiners running at higher capacities to build heating oil stocks, lent support, traders said.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $25.80-90 a barrel, up about five cents from Friday's late cash levels.
The Nov/Dec spread fluctuated within a 38-45 cent range, keeping WTI/Cushing Posting Plus mostly locked in a range. The grade traded between postings plus $2.11 and $2.15 a barrel.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James rose to WTI plus 71 cents a barrel, up from the morning's 67/68 cents.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire climbed to WTI plus 75 cents, up from 72 cents transacted on Friday.
But heavy, sour grades drifted lower hurt by perception of more supplies from Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) sales.
Traders said the deadline for bids into the government's SPR sale tender today dampened West Texas Sour/Midland, as the new sale involved some 15 million barrels of sour crude.
West Texas Sour/Midland dropped to minus $1.60 a barrel, down about 15 cents from Friday, but pared losses later.
The grade recovered to WTI minus $1.53 a barrel in late trade, but traders said there were more sellers willing to sell ahead of Friday's Nov pipeline scheduling deadline.
Congress requires the U.S. Energy Department to sell $220 million worth of oil to close the budget gap.
Eugene Island, another sour grade, managed to hold steady, trading at WTI minus $1.11, within the same range discussed on Friday, but off from last trades at minus $1.04.
